_about: Clinic heal game `tummy` (H10 Bubbles and burps; docs/modes/clinic-design.md). Ali ate too many sweets at the wedding. A close-up of a round comic belly with six coloured bubbles and a see-through tube up to the mouth: drag a bubble up out of the belly and it floats up the tube to a BURP. The count is Kutchi (hakro to panj; six bubbles are always there). Then a drink: paani / dudh / chai (Cook's confirmed words), three unlabelled pitchers in a shuffled order, one tap = half a glass (adh, level 2+), two = full, a third overflows. Level 3 adds the hot-water bottle and the order (pela ... ne poi ...). Levels are data. English placeholders are marked placeholder: true or [bracketed]; the Kutchi words are reused from data/cook.json and docs/kutchi-grammar-notes.md, nothing invented.

too-many-sweets.english: a tummy ache from too many sweets at the wedding (Ali)

cup.english: a cup (the glass: the drink is chosen in the game from three pitchers)

gurgle.english: Ooh, my tummy! Too many sweets!

1._note: The bubbles (a count of six) + the drink by name (any amount). Lines one at a time: the drink row appears when the bubbles close.

2._note: + the amount: 'Ne poi adh {drink}' (half: one tap) or 'Ne poi {drink}' (full: two taps). All rows as one list up front.

3._note: + the hot-water bottle and a random order of the last two steps: 'Pela [the bottle]', 'Ne poi {drink}' or 'Pela {drink}', 'Ne poi [the bottle]'. The second row is right only if its step was done second.
